description: A composite figure of four images that together make one argument about the weight-saving potential of low-density Fe-Al steels in a car body. Two of the images are finite-element screenshots of a transparent wireframe body-in-white of a four-door passenger car in three-quarter front view: (a) highlights the left and right front side members in solid blue, (b) highlights the two A-pillar components in solid red; neither FE panel carries a scale bar, axis or annotation text. Beside each FE model is a data table, both with three columns headed DP600 Ref., FeAl α + γ and FeAl γ and rows for Thickness, Total Mass / vehicle (kg) and Weight saving / vehicle in kg and %. For the front side member (a), thicknesses (Fr / Rr) are 1.7 / 2.1, 1.5 / 1.8 and 1.3 / 1.7 mm, masses 5.88, 4.63 and 3.99 kg, savings 1.25 kg (21%) and 1.89 kg (32%). For the A-Pillar (b), thicknesses are 1.6, 1.4 and 1.25 mm, masses 6.11, 4.84 and 4.12 kg, savings 1.27 kg (21%) and 1.99 kg (33%). The figure demonstrates ~20% (α + γ) and ~30-33% (γ) mass reduction versus DP600 on both parts.

observations.observation: Two panels are FE-model screenshots of a transparent wireframe passenger-car body-in-white; in the first the front side members are solid blue and in the second the A-pillar components are solid red.
Both tables use the same three column headers printed exactly as 'DP600 Ref.', 'FeAl α + γ' and 'FeAl γ'.
Front side member, row 'Thickness Fr / Rr (mm)': 1.7 / 2.1 for DP600 Ref., 1.5 / 1.8 for FeAl α + γ, 1.3 / 1.7 for FeAl γ.
Front side member, row 'Total Mass / vehicle (kg)': 5.88 for DP600 Ref., 4.63 for FeAl α + γ, 3.99 for FeAl γ.
A-Pillar, row 'Thickness (mm)': 1.6 for DP600 Ref., 1.4 for FeAl α + γ, 1.25 for FeAl γ; 'Total Mass / vehicle (kg)': 6.11, 4.84 and 4.12 respectively.
Weight saving per vehicle for the front side member is 1.25 kg (21 %) for FeAl α + γ and 1.89 kg (32 %) for FeAl γ, with the DP600 Ref. column showing '-' (basis of comparison).
Weight saving per vehicle for the A-Pillar is 1.27 kg (21 %) for FeAl α + γ and 1.99 kg (33 %) for FeAl γ, again with '-' in the DP600 Ref. column.

The caption titles the figure 'Calculated weight-saving potential of austenite-ferrite and austenitic lightweight steels versus DP600 for (a) front side member and (b) A-Pillar', identifying the blue parts as the front side member and the red parts as the A-Pillar.
The caption embeds the two tables, i.e. the thickness, total mass and weight-saving values are asserted by the caption text as well as visible in the table images.

The citing text states the simulations are finite-element front crash simulations of a full vehicle (EuroNCAP 40% overlap front crash) performed with LS-DYNA and materials modelled by piecewise linear plasticity (MAT_024) based on experimental tensile data.

The citing text identifies the two lightweight alloys as austenite-ferrite 7.4Al-8.2Mn-0.2C wt.% (YS 646 MPa, UTS 800 MPa, TEL 26%) and fully austenitic 9.3Al-25.8Mn-0.96C wt.% (YS 812 MPa, UTS 1027 MPa, TEL 32%); these compositions and tensile values are not printed in the figure.

The citing text states component thicknesses were adapted to match DP600 reference performance in energy absorption and section forces, and that cost estimation (€/kg saved) for austenite-ferrite was similar to less alloyed concepts (not shown in the figure).
